Bangkok Airways flies Phuket to Koh Samui about 6–8 times a day in about an hour, and Krabi to Samui 1–2 times a day in 45–50 minutes. Overland, joint van-or-bus-and-ferry tickets via Surat Thani and Donsak pier take about 5–6.5 hours from Krabi and 6.5–10 hours from Phuket, for roughly 400–1,500 THB. There is no ferry between Phuket and Samui. The two coasts have opposite monsoons: the Andaman side is wettest from May to October, Samui from October to December.

Good to know: prices and times were last checked on 1 November 2026. Overland fares vary between sellers and change with fuel prices; re-check on the day.

Flights from Phuket and Krabi

Bangkok Airways is the only airline flying nonstop from Phuket or Krabi to Samui. It owns Samui airport, so there is little competition and fares are higher than on Bangkok routes of similar length.

  • Phuket–Samui: about 6–8 flights a day, roughly 07:30–19:00, about 1 hour gate to gate. Frequency is cut in the low season (as few as 6 a day from the late-October schedule change) and rises to about 8 in December.
  • Krabi–Samui: 1–2 flights a day, about 45–50 minutes, typically around midday.
  • Fares: Phuket–Samui from about 3,700 THB in October and November, often 5,000 THB or more in December; Krabi–Samui from about 3,400 THB. Economy fares include a checked bag.
  • Book early for December–January: the turboprop and small-jet flights on these routes sell out first.
  • Watch for connections: booking sites also list one-stop itineraries via Bangkok on low-cost airlines that take 5–10 hours. Check that your flight is nonstop.

Phuket airport is about 50 minutes from Patong and an hour from Kata, so allow 3 hours before departure from the southern beaches. On Samui, the airport is 10–15 minutes from Chaweng; see our Koh Samui airport guide for taxi prices.

Overland joint tickets via Surat Thani

All overland routes cross the peninsula to Donsak pier near Surat Thani, then take a ferry to Nathon or Lipa Noi on Samui's west coast. Departure points in Phuket are usually Phuket Bus Terminal 2 or the operator's town office; many tickets include a hotel pickup from Patong, Kata, Karon and other beaches for an extra fee.

Good to know: overland tickets are timed to specific ferries. If the bus or van runs late, the operator normally moves you to the next sailing; the last Raja ferry from Donsak is at about 19:00. Keep valuables with you, not in the luggage hold.

From Krabi and Ao Nang

Krabi is closer to Donsak than Phuket. Van-and-ferry tickets leave Krabi Town and Ao Nang between about 07:00 and 13:00, take 5–6.5 hours and cost roughly 400–850 THB depending on hotel pickup and whether the boat is a car ferry or a catamaran. Some operators continue to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao on the same ticket. The full Donsak leg is explained on Surat Thani to Koh Samui.

Khao Lak and Khao Sok routes

Khao Lak has no airport. Fly from Phuket (80–100 minutes by road from Khao Lak) or take a van east across Route 401 via Takua Pa and Khao Sok to Surat Thani, then the ferry from Donsak.

Khao Sok National Park lies on that same road, roughly halfway between the Andaman coast and Surat Thani. It is a good stopover between the two coasts: limestone cliffs, rainforest and Cheow Lan Lake. From Samui it is 4–6 hours each way, so do not try it as a day trip. Plan at least 2 days and 1 night, ideally with a night on or near the lake. Vans from Khao Sok to Surat Thani take about 2–2.5 hours, and many connect with the afternoon ferries to Samui, so you can reach the island the same day if you leave Khao Sok in the morning. A sensible route is Phuket or Khao Lak → Khao Sok (2–3 nights) → Surat Thani → Donsak → Samui.

Combining the Andaman and the Gulf by season

This is the main reason to combine Phuket or Krabi with Samui: when one coast is wet, the other is often fine. The Andaman coast takes the south-west monsoon from about May to October; Samui and the Gulf islands take the north-east monsoon from about October to December. Samui's figures below are 1991–2020 averages for the Ko Samui weather station; the Andaman column shows the general seasonal pattern.

The sweet spot for a two-coast trip is January to April, when both are dry. From May to September, spend more of your time on Samui. In November, favour the Andaman side and keep Samui for later. Month-by-month detail is on our Koh Samui weather page, and live wind on windy.com.

Sample two-coast routes

10 days, January to April

  1. Days 1–4 Phuket or Krabi: beaches and an Andaman island day.
  2. Day 5 Fly Phuket → Samui (about 1 h), or take the overland route via Donsak.
  3. Days 6–9 Samui: an Ang Thong boat day, Pig Island, the Big Buddha and Fisherman's Village.
  4. Day 10 Fly home from Samui via Bangkok or Singapore.

14 days with Khao Sok

  1. Days 1–4 Khao Lak or Phuket.
  2. Days 5–6 Van to Khao Sok; a night on or near Cheow Lan Lake.
  3. Day 7 Van to Surat Thani and Donsak, ferry to Samui.
  4. Days 8–11 Samui.
  5. Days 12–13 Koh Phangan or Koh Tao by ferry.
  6. Day 14 Back to Samui for the flight home, with a buffer if the sea is rough.

Choose a base on Samui with where to stay on Koh Samui; for the islands beyond, see Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and Koh Samui to Koh Tao.

Driving yourself

Phuket to Donsak is roughly 5 hours by car via Route 401 across the peninsula, then about 1.5 hours on the Raja or Seatran car ferry. Seatran charges approx. 550–670 THB for a car including the driver in 2026. Rental cars from Phuket or Krabi are often not insured for ferry crossings or island use, and one-way drop fees can be high, so ask before you book. Route 401 is a winding, hilly road through Khao Sok with heavy trucks; avoid driving it at night. Our car rental guide explains Thai insurance and the ferry clause.

Phuket, Krabi or Samui: how they differ

  • Phuket is bigger and busier, with more nightlife, more flights and a wide spread of beaches.
  • Krabi and Ao Nang are known for limestone cliffs, rock climbing and island-hopping by longtail.
  • Samui has calmer sea for most of the year, an easier ring road, upmarket villas, and boat trips to Ang Thong, Pig Island, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. Our Koh Samui travel guide covers the island in full.

Arriving on Samui

  • By air: kiosk taxis from the airport cost approx. 400–700 THB by zone; Chaweng is 10–15 minutes away.
  • At Nathon pier: songthaews run by day around the ring road (locals pay about 60–80 THB to Chaweng); taxis cost roughly 600–1,000 THB.
  • At Lipa Noi (Raja): take a taxi or a hotel-drop minibus; few songthaews pass the port.

Plan your days with our Koh Samui itinerary and getting around Koh Samui guides.

What to do once you are on Samui

If you arrive in the Andaman's wet season (May–October), Samui's sea is usually at its best for boat trips. Our Ang Thong speedboat day tour (1,800 THB adult, 1,400 THB child) runs from 16 December to 31 October; the park is closed from 1 November to 15 December. The Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip (2,200 THB adult, plus the 250 THB island fee) shows you another island without moving hotels. Pig Island tours run every day of the year. All tours include hotel pickup from most areas of Koh Samui.
